about: Trainchecker 'Your train passes near…'. One item per stretch between neighbouring stations, keyed by the stretch's id (its two station codes in alphabetical order). network holds every station and every stretch with any of it in England, as [a, b, length in metres], from stretches.json (OpenStreetMap, © OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database Licence). In an item, a and b are the stretch in the direction the research was done; side is the side of the train when travelling from a to b (facing forwards): swap left and right for b to a. text has {side} for 'left' or 'right'; textReverse, where present, replaces text for b to a. England only. Every fact checked against its source.

PNZ-SER.name: Penzance Heliport
PNZ-SER.text: Your train passes near Penzance Heliport, on the train's {side}, where helicopters to the Isles of Scilly started flying again in 2020 after an eight-year gap.

LTS-SER.name: St Erth station
LTS-SER.text: St Erth station, at one end of this stretch, is listed Grade II and is the junction for the St Ives Bay Line.

HYL-SER.name: Harvey & Co foundry, Hayle
HYL-SER.text: Your train passes the old offices of Harvey & Co, on the train's {side}, the foundry John Harvey set up in Hayle in 1779.

CBN-HYL.name: Trevithick Cottage
CBN-HYL.text: Your train passes near Trevithick Cottage, on the train's {side}, childhood home of the Cornish engineer Richard Trevithick, now cared for by the National Trust.

CBN-RED.name: Carn Brea
CBN-RED.text: Your train passes near the hill of Carn Brea, on the train's {side}, with a Neolithic enclosure, a medieval castle and old mine workings on it.

RED-TRU.name: Wheal Busy
RED-TRU.text: Your train passes near Wheal Busy, on the train's {side}, a mine that produced huge amounts of copper in the 18th century, now part of the Cornish mining World Heritage Site.

PRW-TRU.name: Carnon Viaduct
PRW-TRU.text: Your train crosses Carnon Viaduct, 96 feet high, over Restronguet Creek. The first viaduct here had timber on stone piers; a new stone viaduct replaced it in 1933.

PRW-PYN.name: Ponsanooth Viaduct
PRW-PYN.text: Your train crosses Ponsanooth Viaduct over the River Kennal. At 139 feet high, it is the tallest viaduct west of Truro.

PNM-PYN.name: Collegewood Viaduct
PNM-PYN.text: Your train crosses Collegewood Viaduct, 954 feet long. When it was rebuilt in stone in 1934, it was the last timber viaduct in Cornwall to be replaced; the piers of the old one still stand.

FMT-PNM.name: National Maritime Museum Cornwall
FMT-PNM.text: Your train passes near the National Maritime Museum Cornwall, on the train's {side}, in a harbourside building that opened in February 2003. It looks after the National Small Boat Collection, which came from the National Maritime Museum in Greenwich.

FAL-FMT.name: Pendennis Castle
FAL-FMT.text: Your train passes near Pendennis Castle, on the train's {side}, an artillery fort built for Henry VIII between 1540 and 1542. In the Civil War its Royalist garrison held out through a long siege until August 1646.

SAU-TRU.name: Truro Cathedral
SAU-TRU.text: Your train passes near Truro Cathedral, on the train's {side}, built between 1880 and 1910 on the site of St Mary's parish church.

PAR-SAU.name: Charlestown
PAR-SAU.text: Your train passes near Charlestown harbour, on the train's {side}, a port that grew in the late 18th century from the fishing village of West Polmear and has changed little since.

LUX-PAR.name: Treffry Viaduct
LUX-PAR.text: Your train passes beneath the Treffry Viaduct, built of granite by Joseph Treffry between 1839 and 1842 to carry his tramway, and water for his Fowey Consols mine, across the Luxulyan Valley.

BGL-LUX.name: Luxulyan
BGL-LUX.text: Your train passes near Luxulyan, on the train's {side}, which gives its name to luxulyanite, a rare Cornish granite used for the Duke of Wellington's sarcophagus in St Paul's Cathedral.

BGL-ROC.name: Holy well north-west of Roche station
BGL-ROC.text: Your train passes near an old holy well north-west of Roche station, on the train's {side}, protected as a scheduled monument.

ROC-SCR.name: Goss Moor
ROC-SCR.text: Your train crosses Goss Moor, a national nature reserve and the largest continuous mire in south-west Britain. The A30 once ran through the middle of it.

QUI-SCR.name: St Columb Road station
QUI-SCR.text: St Columb Road station, at one end of this stretch, was first called Halloon; it took its present name in 1878. It is a request stop.

NQY-QUI.name: Trenance Viaduct
NQY-QUI.text: Your train crosses Trenance Viaduct, 141 metres long, over the Trenance valley in Newquay. The first, of timber on stone piers, opened in 1849; today's masonry viaduct dates from 1939.

LOS-PAR.name: Duchy Palace, Lostwithiel
LOS-PAR.text: Your train passes near the Duchy Palace in Lostwithiel, on the train's {side}, once the centre from which the Dukes of Cornwall ran their estates.

BOD-LOS.name: Restormel Castle
BOD-LOS.text: Your train passes near Restormel Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman castle known for its perfectly circular design.

BOD-LSK.name: Moorswater Viaduct
BOD-LSK.text: Your train crosses Moorswater Viaduct. Beside it stand the stone piers of the earlier viaduct, which carried the line on timber, as Brunel advised for Cornwall's valleys.

COE-LSK.name: Liskeard Viaduct
COE-LSK.text: Your train passes beneath Liskeard Viaduct, 150 feet high, which carries the main line. The Looe branch has run under it since 1901.

COE-SKN.name: Coombe Junction Halt
COE-SKN.text: At Coombe Junction Halt, at one end of this stretch, trains between Liskeard and Looe change direction: the driver and guard swap ends.

CAU-SKN.name: St Keyne Wishing Well Halt
CAU-SKN.text: St Keyne Wishing Well Halt, at one end of this stretch, shares its name with St Keyne's holy well. In Victorian times it was said that whichever of a newly married couple drank from it first would have the upper hand.

CAU-SDP.name: Liskeard and Looe Union Canal
CAU-SDP.text: Your train runs along the valley of the East Looe River, beside the remains of the Liskeard and Looe Union Canal. It was finished in 1828 with 24 locks, and fell out of use after the railway was built in 1860.

LOO-SDP.name: Old Guildhall, Looe
LOO-SDP.text: Your train passes near the Old Guildhall in East Looe, on the train's {side}, believed to date from around 1450.

LSK-MEN.name: St Martin's Church, Liskeard
LSK-MEN.text: Your train passes near St Martin's Church, Liskeard, on the train's {side}, the second-largest parish church in Cornwall.

MEN-SGM.name: St Germans Priory
MEN-SGM.text: Your train passes near St Germans church, on the train's {side}, once the seat of the Saxon bishops of Cornwall.

SGM-STS.name: Trematon Castle
SGM-STS.text: Your train passes near Trematon Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman motte-and-bailey castle with a 12th-century keep, overlooking the River Lynher.

LEL-LTS.name: Lelant Saltings
LEL-LTS.text: Your train runs beside Lelant Saltings, on the train's {side}, part of the Hayle Estuary, where the RSPB manages a nature reserve.

CBB-LEL.name: St Uny's Church, Lelant
CBB-LEL.text: Your train passes Lelant's parish church of St Uny, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I, with Norman work in its nave arcades.

CBB-SIV.name: Barbara Hepworth Museum
CBB-SIV.text: Your train passes near Trewyn Studio, on the train's {side}, which the sculptor Barbara Hepworth bought in 1949. She lived and worked there until her death in 1975; it is now a museum and sculpture garden.

CSK-GSL.name: Morwellham Quay
CSK-GSL.text: Your train passes near Morwellham Quay, on the train's {side} across the Tamar in Devon, a river port that grew up to serve the local mines. It is now an open-air museum.

BAS-CSK.name: Calstock Viaduct
BAS-CSK.text: Your train crosses the Tamar between Devon and Cornwall on Calstock Viaduct, 120 feet high, with 12 arches built from 11,148 concrete blocks between 1904 and 1907.

BAS-BFE.name: St Andrew's Church, Bere Ferrers
BAS-BFE.text: Your train passes near St Andrew's Church in Bere Ferrers, on the train's {side}, whose stained glass is the oldest in Devon outside Exeter Cathedral.

BFE-SBV.name: Tavy Bridge
BFE-SBV.text: Your train crosses the mouth of the River Tavy, just before it joins the Tamar, on the Tavy Bridge, 453 metres long.

SBF-SBV.name: St Budeaux connection
SBF-SBV.text: Your train uses a link between the two railways at St Budeaux, put in on March 21st 1941 so that trains could get round bomb damage. Since 1964, when the old line into Devonport closed, all trains from Victoria Road have used it.

KEY-SBF.name: HMS Drake
KEY-SBF.text: Your train passes near HMS Drake, on the train's {side}: not a ship but a "stone frigate", the naval barracks for Devonport.

DOC-KEY.name: HMNB Devonport
DOC-KEY.text: Your train passes near Devonport naval base, on the train's {side}, the largest naval base in Western Europe.

DOC-DPT.name: Devonport Park
DOC-DPT.text: Your train passes near Devonport Park, on the train's {side}, laid out in the 1850s on former military land.

DPT-PLY.name: Mount Pleasant Redoubt
DPT-PLY.text: Your train passes near Mount Pleasant Redoubt, on the train's {side}, an earthwork fort built around 1780 to guard the dockyard against a French and Spanish invasion.

IVY-PLY.name: Saltram House
IVY-PLY.text: Your train passes near Saltram House, on the train's {side}, which Nikolaus Pevsner called "the most impressive country house in Devon", with interiors by Robert Adam.

IVY-TOT.name: Totnes Castle
IVY-TOT.text: Your train passes near Totnes Castle, on the train's {side}, one of the best-preserved Norman motte-and-bailey castles in England.

NTA-TOT.name: Forde House, Newton Abbot
NTA-TOT.text: Your train passes near Forde House, on the train's {side}, a manor house of about 1550, enlarged around 1610 and known for its 17th-century carving and plasterwork.

NTA-TGM.name: Shaldon
NTA-TGM.text: Your train runs beside the Teign estuary, with the village of Shaldon across the water on the train's {side}.

NTA-TRR.name: Forde House
NTA-TRR.text: Your train passes near Forde House, on the train's {side}, enlarged around 1610. Charles I stayed there in 1625, and William of Orange in 1688, a few days after landing at Brixham.

TQY-TRR.name: Torre Abbey
TQY-TRR.text: Your train passes near Torre Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded in 1196 for Premonstratensian canons and now the best-preserved medieval monastery in Devon and Cornwall.

PGN-TQY.name: Oldway Mansion
PGN-TQY.text: Your train passes near Oldway Mansion, on the train's {side}, built for the sewing-machine maker Isaac Singer and rebuilt by his son Paris in the style of the Palace of Versailles.

DWL-TGM.name: Parson and Clerk
DWL-TGM.text: As your train goes through Parson's Tunnel, the two rock stacks it is named after, the Parson and Clerk, stand just off the headland on the train's {side}.

DWL-DWW.name: Langstone Rock
DWL-DWW.text: Your train passes Langstone Rock, on the train's {side}, a red sandstone headland that the sea, and then Brunel's railway, cut off from the mainland.

DWW-SCS.name: Starcross Pumping House
DWW-SCS.text: Your train passes Brunel's pumping house at Starcross, on the train's {side}, built in 1845 for his atmospheric railway, whose trains ran for less than a year. It is the only complete pumping house left from the three atmospheric lines in the British Isles.

MBT-SCS.name: Powderham Castle
MBT-SCS.text: Your train passes near Powderham Castle, on the train's {side}, a fortified manor house on the bank of the Exe estuary, listed Grade I.

EXT-MBT.name: Custom House, Exeter
EXT-MBT.text: Your train passes near Exeter's Custom House, on the train's {side}, built in the late 17th century, the first in England built for the purpose.

EXD-EXT.name: Exeter Cathedral
EXD-EXT.text: Your train passes near Exeter Cathedral, on the train's {side}, complete by about 1400, with the longest unbroken medieval stone-vaulted ceiling in the world.

EXD-NTC.name: Cowley Bridge
EXD-NTC.text: Your train passes near Cowley Bridge, on the train's {side}, a three-arched classical bridge built in 1813 and 1814 by James Green, surveyor to the county of Devon.

CDI-NTC.name: Church of St Cyriac and St Julitta, Newton St Cyres
CDI-NTC.text: Your train passes near the parish church of Newton St Cyres, on the train's {side}, built in the 15th century of a reddish local volcanic stone. Inside is a standing effigy of John Northcote, who died in 1632.

CDI-YEO.name: Church of the Holy Cross, Crediton
CDI-YEO.text: Your train passes near Crediton's Church of the Holy Cross, on the train's {side}, on the site of the cathedral of the bishops of Crediton until the see moved to Exeter in 1050.

OKI-YEO.name: Roman forts at North Tawton
OKI-YEO.text: Your train passes near the site of Roman forts at North Tawton, on the train's {side}, where the Romans crossed the River Taw. The fort is thought to have been called Nemetostatio.

OKE-OKI.name: Okehampton Castle
OKE-OKI.text: Your train passes near Okehampton Castle, on the train's {side}, built between 1068 and 1086 after a revolt in Devon against Norman rule. It is now a ruin.

COP-YEO.name: Copplestone Cross
COP-YEO.text: Your train passes Copplestone Cross, on the train's {side}, an ancient carved granite pillar listed Grade I, standing where three old parishes meet.

COP-MRD.name: Church of St Mary the Virgin, Down St Mary
COP-MRD.text: Your train passes near the church of St Mary the Virgin at Down St Mary, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I and rebuilt in the 1400s. One of the two old crosses in its churchyard was found being used as a paving slab in Bow, and put back up between 1897 and 1909.

LAP-MRD.name: Roman fort at Bury Barton
LAP-MRD.text: Your train passes near the site of a Roman fort at Bury Barton, on the train's {side}, thought to be a large early fort that was followed by a smaller one.

EGG-LAP.name: Church of St Thomas of Canterbury, Lapford
EGG-LAP.text: Your train passes near Lapford's church of St Thomas of Canterbury, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I. Inside is a late 15th-century screen, carved on both sides.

EGG-KGN.name: Gatehouse at Colleton
EGG-KGN.text: Your train passes near the gatehouse at Colleton, on the train's {side}, probably from the 1400s and listed Grade I. Its upper floor was once a chapel, licensed in 1402.

KGN-PMA.name: Kings Nympton station
KGN-PMA.text: Kings Nympton station, at one end of this stretch, opened in 1854 as South Molton Road. It was renamed in 1951 to avoid confusion with South Molton station on the line to Taunton.

PMA-UMB.name: Brightley Barton
PMA-UMB.text: Your train passes near Brightley Barton, on the train's {side}, on a hillside above the River Taw. From the early 1500s to 1715 it was the seat of the Giffard family, and the medieval stone walls of their house's moat still survive, a great rarity in North Devon.

CPN-UMB.name: Umberleigh House and Holy Trinity Chapel
CPN-UMB.text: Your train passes near Umberleigh House, on the train's {side}, a Georgian farmhouse listed Grade I with the ruins of the medieval chapel of the Holy Trinity beside it. The Devon historian Tristram Risdon wrote that the site was once a palace of the Saxon king Æthelstan.

BNP-CPN.name: Barnstaple Long Bridge
BNP-CPN.text: Your train passes near Barnstaple's Long Bridge over the River Taw, on the train's {side}, one of the largest medieval bridges in Britain. A will of 1274 left money for its upkeep.

EXC-EXD.name: Rougemont Castle
EXC-EXD.text: Your train passes near Rougemont Castle, on the train's {side}, built into a corner of Exeter's Roman walls from 1068, after the city rebelled against William the Conqueror. In 1682 the three Devon Witches, the last people in England executed for witchcraft, were tried there.

EXD-TVP.name: St Andrew's Church, Cullompton
EXD-TVP.text: Your train passes near St Andrew's Church, Cullompton, on the train's {side}, mostly 15th-century and known for its fan-vaulted Lane Aisle.

TAU-TVP.name: Tonedale Mills, Wellington
TAU-TVP.text: Your train passes near Tonedale Mills in Wellington, on the train's {side}, the largest textile mill in South West England, famous for Taunton serge and later the khaki cloth and puttees of the British Army.

BWT-TAU.name: Taunton Castle
BWT-TAU.text: Your train passes near Taunton Castle, on the train's {side}, now the Museum of Somerset. In its Great Hall in 1685 Judge Jeffreys held the Bloody Assizes after the Monmouth Rebellion, and 144 men were hanged.

CLC-TAU.name: Athelney
CLC-TAU.text: Your train passes near Athelney, on the train's {side}, where Alfred the Great hid before defeating the Vikings at Edington in 878, and where he later founded an abbey.

CLC-YVP.name: Haynes Motor Museum
CLC-YVP.text: Your train passes near the Haynes Motor Museum at Sparkford, on the train's {side}, with more than 300 cars and motorcycles. It was founded in 1985 by John Haynes, of the Haynes workshop manuals, in a disused sawmill.

THO-YVP.name: Newton Surmaville
THO-YVP.text: Your train passes near Newton Surmaville, on the train's {side}, a house built between 1608 and 1612 for the clothier Robert Harbin and listed Grade I.

THO-YET.name: Upbury Farm, Yetminster
THO-YET.text: Your train passes near Upbury Farm in Yetminster, on the train's {side}, where a blue plaque remembers the farmer Benjamin Jesty, born in the village. In 1774, some 20 years before Edward Jenner's vaccine, he used cowpox to give immunity against smallpox.

CNO-YET.name: St Andrew's Church, Yetminster
CNO-YET.text: Your train passes near St Andrew's Church in Yetminster, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I and mostly from the mid-1400s. Its faceless clock, some 300 years old, chimes the national anthem every three hours.

CNO-MDN.name: Church of St Peter and St Paul, Cattistock
CNO-MDN.text: Your train passes near the church at Cattistock, on the train's {side}, rebuilt in the 1800s by Sir George Gilbert Scott and his son. The son's tall tower earned it the name "Cathedral of the Frome Valley".

DCW-MDN.name: Poundbury Camp
DCW-MDN.text: Your train runs in a tunnel beneath Poundbury Camp, an Iron Age hillfort above Dorchester. Brunel wanted a cutting through it, but local outrage meant the more expensive tunnel was built instead.

DCW-UPW.name: Maumbury Rings
DCW-UPW.text: Your train passes near Maumbury Rings, on the train's {side}, a Neolithic henge that the Romans made into an amphitheatre and the Civil War into an artillery fort. In 1846 the route planned for the Southampton and Dorchester Railway was changed to spare it.

DCH-UPW.name: Ridgeway Hill Viking burial pit
DCH-UPW.text: Your train passes near Ridgeway Hill, on the train's {side}, where in June 2009 archaeologists found a pit holding the remains of 54 Scandinavian men, executed some time between 970 and 1025. They are thought to have been Vikings killed by the local Anglo-Saxons.

UPW-WEY.name: King's Statue, Weymouth
UPW-WEY.text: Your train passes near the King's Statue in Weymouth, on the train's {side}, put up in 1809 for George III's Golden Jubilee. The king came to Weymouth on holiday 14 times, the first in 1789.

BRU-CLC.name: Bruton Dovecote
BRU-CLC.text: Your train passes near the Bruton Dovecote, on the train's {side}, a stone tower built between the 15th and 17th centuries that may have been a lookout before it housed pigeons.

BRU-FRO.name: Marston Moat
BRU-FRO.text: Your train passes near Marston Moat, on the train's {side}, the moat of a fortified manor house held by the Bigot family before 1195. There is some evidence they fortified it without the king's licence; that, and an insult to the king's messenger, cost Richard Bigot his lands.

FRO-WSB.name: Berkley House
FRO-WSB.text: Your train passes near Berkley House, on the train's {side}, home of Squire Thomas Prowse, who built the church of St Mary beside it in 1751. The church has a glazed cupola over its nave.

TRO-WSB.name: Handle House, Studley Mills
TRO-WSB.text: Your train passes near the Handle House at Studley Mills in Trowbridge, on the train's {side}, which straddles the River Biss. It was used to dry and store teasels, which were used to raise the nap of cloth.

BOA-TRO.name: Bradford-on-Avon Tithe Barn
BOA-TRO.text: Your train passes near the tithe barn at Barton Farm, on the train's {side}, built in the 1330s for the nuns of Shaftesbury Abbey, the richest nunnery in England. It is listed Grade I and looked after by English Heritage.

AVF-BOA.name: St Laurence's Church, Bradford-on-Avon
AVF-BOA.text: Your train passes near St Laurence's Church in Bradford-on-Avon, on the train's {side}, one of very few Anglo-Saxon churches in England without later medieval changes. For many years it was used as a school and a cottage, until William Jones, rector of the parish church of Holy Trinity, rediscovered it in 1856.

AVF-FFD.name: Avoncliff Aqueduct
AVF-FFD.text: Your train passes under Avoncliff Aqueduct, next to Avoncliff station, which carries the Kennet and Avon Canal over the River Avon and the railway. It was built by John Rennie and John Thomas between 1797 and 1801.

BTH-FFD.name: Claverton Pumping Station
BTH-FFD.text: Your train passes near Claverton Pumping Station, on the train's {side}, built by John Rennie between 1809 and 1813. The River Avon turns its great water wheel, which pumps water 48 feet up to the Kennet and Avon Canal, on the other side of the railway.

BTH-OLF.name: Roman Baths
BTH-OLF.text: Your train passes near the Roman Baths, on the train's {side}, where the Romans built a temple at the hot spring between AD 60 and 70.

KYN-OLF.name: Saltford Brass Mill
KYN-OLF.text: Your train passes near Saltford Brass Mill, on the train's {side}, the last survivor of more than 30 mills that once worked along this stretch of the Avon.

BTH-CPM.name: Central Government War Headquarters, Corsham
BTH-CPM.text: While your train is in Box Tunnel, the government's secret Cold War headquarters, built in an old stone quarry, lies just to the train's {side}.

CPM-MKM.name: Yelde Hall, Chippenham
CPM-MKM.text: Your train passes near the Yelde Hall in Chippenham's Market Place, on the train's {side}, built in about 1450 and once the meeting place of Chippenham Borough Council. It is listed Grade I.

MKM-TRO.name: Staverton Mill
MKM-TRO.text: Your train passes near Staverton Mill, on the train's {side}, a mill on the River Avon since the Domesday Book. Once a woollen mill and later a Nestlé milk factory, it makes breakfast cereals: Shredded Wheat and Shreddies moved there in 2007.

CPM-SWI.name: STEAM, Museum of the Great Western Railway
CPM-SWI.text: Your train passes near STEAM, the Museum of the Great Western Railway, on the train's {side}. It is in a workshop of Swindon Works, built around 1842 with stone from Box Tunnel.

BPW-SWI.name: Health Hydro, Swindon
BPW-SWI.text: Your train passes near the Health Hydro in Swindon, on the train's {side}, built for the Great Western Railway's Medical Fund Society. Its Turkish baths carry on a service begun for railway workers and their families in 1868, the longest-surviving Victorian Turkish baths in the world; in 1948 the fund's medical services became part of the new NHS.

BPW-FIT.name: Stoke Gifford depot
BPW-FIT.text: Your train passes near Stoke Gifford depot, on the train's {side}, built on a triangle of land between three railway lines. It was built to look after Great Western Railway's Class 800 trains, which entered service in 2017.

ASD-FIT.name: New Orphan Houses, Ashley Down
ASD-FIT.text: Your train passes near the New Orphan Houses on Ashley Down, on the train's {side}, built between 1849 and 1870 by George Müller. Their five houses held 2,050 children at a time, and Müller never asked anyone for money to run them.

ASD-SRD.name: St Werburgh's Church, Bristol
ASD-SRD.text: Your train passes near St Werburgh's Church, on the train's {side}, a medieval church that stood in Corn Street in the old city until 1879, when it was taken down and rebuilt here. Its 14th-century tower was moved stone by stone; the church is now a climbing centre.

MTP-SRD.name: St Paul's Church, Bristol
MTP-SRD.text: Your train passes near St Paul's Church in Portland Square, on the train's {side}, begun in 1789 and listed Grade I. It closed in 1988 and is now Circomedia, a circus school.

MTP-RDA.name: Redland Chapel
MTP-RDA.text: Your train passes near Redland Chapel, on the train's {side}, built in 1742 as a private chapel for John Cossins of Redland Court and listed Grade I. Now the parish church, it is unusual in having no patron saint.

CFN-RDA.name: Clifton Lido
CFN-RDA.text: Your train passes near the Lido in Clifton, on the train's {side}, opened as the Clifton Victoria Baths in 1850. It closed in 1990 and was considered for demolition, but was restored and reopened in 2008.

CFN-SML.name: Abona Roman town
CFN-SML.text: Your train runs through the site of Abona, a small Roman port town at the mouth of the River Trym. Much Roman material was dug up when the dock at Sea Mills was built.

SHH-SML.name: Kings Weston House
SHH-SML.text: Your train passes near Kings Weston House, on the train's {side}, built between 1712 and 1719 to designs by Sir John Vanbrugh for the lawyer and politician Edward Southwell.

PRI-SHH.name: Avonmouth Bridge
PRI-SHH.text: Your train passes near the Avonmouth Bridge, on the train's {side}, which carries the M5 over the River Avon. It is 4,554 feet long, with a main span of 538 feet.

AVN-PRI.name: Pill Lifeboat Station
AVN-PRI.text: Your train passes near Pill, across the river on the train's {side}, where the RNLI kept a lifeboat for little more than three years, from July 1971 to November 1974.

AVN-SAR.name: Avonmouth Docks
AVN-SAR.text: Your train passes near Avonmouth Docks, on the train's {side}, part of the Port of Bristol where the Avon meets the Severn estuary. Today they are one of the UK's main ports for chilled foods, especially fruit and vegetables.

SAR-SVB.name: Lawrence Weston Wind Turbine
SAR-SVB.text: Your train passes near the Lawrence Weston wind turbine, on the train's {side}, owned by the community it helps to fund. When it started turning in May 2023 it was the tallest onshore wind turbine in England, 150 metres to the tip of its blades.

LWH-SRD.name: Northern Storm Water Interceptor
LWH-SRD.text: Your train passes near Bristol's Northern Storm Water Interceptor, on the train's {side}: a tunnel about 16 feet across that carries floodwater from the River Frome at Eastville three miles under the city to the Avon Gorge. It was finished in 1962.

BRI-LWH.name: Brunel's Old Station, Temple Meads
BRI-LWH.text: Your train passes near Brunel's original Temple Meads station, on the train's {side}, opened on August 31st 1840 as the western end of the Great Western Railway. It is listed Grade I and no longer used by trains.

BMT-BRI.name: St Mary Redcliffe
BMT-BRI.text: Your train passes near St Mary Redcliffe, on the train's {side}, whose spire is 274 feet high. Elizabeth I is said to have called it "the fairest, goodliest and most famous parish church in England" on a visit in 1574.

BMT-PSN.name: St John the Baptist's Church, Bedminster
BMT-PSN.text: Your train passes near the site of St John the Baptist's Church in Bedminster, on the train's {side}, one of Bristol's oldest churches, first recorded in 1003. It was gutted in the Blitz in November 1940 and in 1967 the council approved the demolition of its ruins.

NLS-PSN.name: Tyntesfield
NLS-PSN.text: Your train passes near the park of Tyntesfield, on the train's {side}, around a Victorian Gothic house remodelled in the 1860s for William Gibbs, whose fortune came from guano. The National Trust bought it in 2002.

DID-SWI.name: Uffington
DID-SWI.text: Your train passes near the village of Uffington, on the train's {side}, where Thomas Hughes, author of Tom Brown's School Days, was born in 1822. The poet John Betjeman lived there from 1934 to 1945.

APF-DID.name: Didcot Railway Centre
APF-DID.text: Your train passes Didcot Railway Centre, on the train's {side}, a railway museum in what was once a Great Western Railway engine shed.

APF-CUM.name: Appleford Railway Bridge
APF-CUM.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Appleford Railway Bridge. The first bridge here, of timber, was finished in 1844; today's steel one dates from 1927.

CUM-RAD.name: Culham fusion research site
CUM-RAD.text: Your train passes near the Culham fusion research site, on the train's {side}. Its Joint European Torus began work in 1983 and in 1991 became the first reactor in the world to run on the deuterium and tritium fuel meant for future power stations.

OXF-RAD.name: St Mary the Virgin, Iffley
OXF-RAD.text: Your train passes near St Mary the Virgin, Iffley, on the train's {side}, built in the second half of the 12th century and one of the best-preserved Norman churches in England.

CHO-DID.name: St Mary's Church, Cholsey
CHO-DID.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church, Cholsey, on the train's {side}, where Agatha Christie is buried.

CHO-GOR.name: Moulsford Railway Bridge
CHO-GOR.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Moulsford Railway Bridge, known locally as Four Arches. Brunel set its brick arches at a slant across the river.

GOR-PAN.name: Basildon Park
GOR-PAN.text: Your train passes near Basildon Park, on the train's {side}, an 18th-century house that played Netherfield, Mr Bingley's home, in the 2005 film of Pride & Prejudice.

PAN-TLH.name: Mapledurham Watermill
PAN-TLH.text: Your train passes near Mapledurham Watermill, on the train's {side} across the Thames, the last working watermill on the river.

RDW-THE.name: Garston Lock
RDW-THE.text: Your train passes near Garston Lock, on the train's {side}, one of only two working turf-sided locks left on the Kennet and Avon Canal. Its sloping grass sides use more water than brick ones.

AMT-THE.name: Folly Farm, Sulhamstead
AMT-THE.text: Your train passes near Folly Farm, on the train's {side}, a house that Edwin Lutyens extended around 1906 and 1912, with gardens he designed with Gertrude Jekyll.

AMT-MDG.name: Aldermaston Lock
AMT-MDG.text: Your train passes near Aldermaston Lock, on the train's {side}, built between 1718 and 1723 and later given unusual scalloped brick walls.

MDG-THA.name: Midgham Lock
MDG-THA.text: Your train passes near Midgham Lock, on the train's {side}, one of the locks built between 1718 and 1723 under the engineer John Hore of Newbury, when the River Kennet was made navigable.

NRC-THA.name: Monkey Marsh Lock
NRC-THA.text: Your train passes near Monkey Marsh Lock, on the train's {side}, a turf-sided lock from the 1720s that is now a scheduled monument.

NBY-NRC.name: West Berkshire Museum
NBY-NRC.text: Your train passes near the West Berkshire Museum, on the train's {side}, partly housed in Newbury's Cloth Hall, built in 1627 as a cloth factory.

KIT-NBY.name: Litten Chapel
KIT-NBY.text: Your train passes near the Litten Chapel, on the train's {side}, an early 16th-century chapel of Newbury's medieval St Bartholomew's hospital, with finely carved timber roof trusses.

HGD-KIT.name: Church of St Mark and St Luke, Avington
HGD-KIT.text: Your train passes near the church of St Mark and St Luke at Avington, on the train's {side}, an unspoilt Norman church listed Grade I.

BDW-HGD.name: Somerset Hospital, Froxfield
BDW-HGD.text: Your train passes near the Somerset Hospital at Froxfield, on the train's {side}: almshouses for widows left by Sarah, Duchess of Somerset, the oldest part built in 1694.

BDW-PEW.name: Crofton Pumping Station
BDW-PEW.text: Your train passes Crofton Pumping Station, on the train's {side}. Its Boulton & Watt steam engine of 1812 is the oldest working beam engine in the world still in its original engine house.

PEW-WSB.name: Edington Priory
PEW-WSB.text: Your train passes near Edington Priory church, on the train's {side}, built by William Edington, Bishop of Winchester, and consecrated in 1361.

RDW-RGP.name: Elm Park (stadium site)
RDW-RGP.text: Your train passes near the site of Elm Park, on the train's {side}, home of Reading Football Club from 1896 to 1998.

BMY-MOR.name: Mortimer station
BMY-MOR.text: Mortimer station, at one end of this stretch, keeps its Brunel-designed Great Western Railway buildings, still in use.

BMY-BSK.name: Holy Ghost Chapel ruins, Basingstoke
BMY-BSK.text: Your train passes near the ruins of the Holy Ghost Chapel, on the train's {side}: a chapel stood here by 1244, and Lord Sandys added a family chapel in 1524.

RDG-RDW.name: Greyfriars Church, Reading
RDG-RDW.text: Your train passes near Greyfriars Church, on the train's {side}, the oldest Franciscan church in the UK still used for worship.

RDG-TWY.name: Reading Abbey
RDG-TWY.text: Your train passes near the ruins of Reading Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded by Henry I in 1121. He was buried there in 1136.

TWY-WGV.name: Loddon Nature Reserve
TWY-WGV.text: Your train passes near Loddon Nature Reserve, on the train's {side}, 14 hectares run by the Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust.

SHI-WGV.name: Hannen Columbarium, Wargrave
SHI-WGV.text: Your train passes near St Mary's churchyard in Wargrave, on the train's {side}, where the Hannen family's columbarium, a resting place for ashes, was designed by Edwin Lutyens.

HOT-SHI.name: Henley Bridge
HOT-SHI.text: Your train passes near Henley Bridge, on the train's {side}, built in 1786 with five stone arches across the Thames.

MAI-TWY.name: Church of St James, Ruscombe
MAI-TWY.text: Your train passes near the Church of St James, Ruscombe, on the train's {side}. Its flint chancel dates from the 12th century; the nave and tower were rebuilt in brick in 1638 and 1639.

MAI-TAP.name: Maidenhead Railway Bridge
MAI-TAP.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Brunel's Maidenhead Railway Bridge, whose two main brick arches are thought to be the longest and flattest ever built. Turner painted a train crossing it in Rain, Steam and Speed (1844).

BNM-TAP.name: Burnham Abbey
BNM-TAP.text: Your train passes near Burnham Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded in 1266 by Richard, Earl of Cornwall, brother of King Henry III. Anglican nuns made it their home from 1916.

BNM-SLO.name: Site of William Herschel's house
BNM-SLO.text: Your train passes near the site of William Herschel's house, on the train's {side}, where he and his sister Caroline built his 40-foot telescope, the largest in the world for 50 years. With it he found two of Saturn's moons in 1789.

LNY-SLO.name: Kedermister Library, St Mary's Church, Langley
LNY-SLO.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church, Langley, on the train's {side}. Inside is the Kedermister Library, a parish library from the 1600s still kept in the painted cupboards made for it in 1620.

IVR-LNY.name: Buckinghamshire and Berkshire
IVR-LNY.text: Between Iver and Langley, your train passes from Buckinghamshire into Berkshire.
IVR-LNY.textReverse: Between Langley and Iver, your train passes from Berkshire into Buckinghamshire.

IVR-WDT.name: River Colne
IVR-WDT.text: Your train crosses the River Colne, and about here passes between Greater London and Buckinghamshire.

HAY-WDT.name: Old Vinyl Factory
HAY-WDT.text: Your train passes near the Old Vinyl Factory, on the train's {side}: EMI's old record works, which pressed vinyl records from 1952 until the 1970s.

AML-EAL.name: Ealing Village
AML-EAL.text: Your train passes near Ealing Village, on the train's {side}: five Art Deco blocks of flats built from 1934 to 1936 to tempt film stars from Ealing Studios. In the end, most of the flats went to film crews.

AML-PAD.name: Kensal Green Cemetery
AML-PAD.text: Your train passes near Kensal Green Cemetery, on the train's {side}, where Isambard Kingdom Brunel, the engineer who built this railway, is buried with his father, Marc.

SBF-STS.name: Royal Albert Bridge
SBF-STS.text: Your train crosses the Tamar from Devon into Cornwall on Brunel's Royal Albert Bridge, its two 455-foot iron spans 100 feet above the water.
SBF-STS.textReverse: Your train crosses the Tamar from Cornwall into Devon on Brunel's Royal Albert Bridge, its two 455-foot iron spans 100 feet above the water.

BRI-KYN.name: Somerdale
BRI-KYN.text: Your train passes near the old Somerdale chocolate factory, on the train's {side}, built for Fry's from 1924 and closed in 2011. Remains of a Roman settlement were found on the site.

BRU-WSB.name: Witham Priory
BRU-WSB.text: Your train passes the site of Witham Priory, on the train's {side}, founded in 1178 or 1179 as the first Carthusian monastery in England.

RDG-TLH.name: Chazey Court Barn
RDG-TLH.text: Your train passes near Chazey Court Barn, on the train's {side} across the Thames: a huge seven-bay brick barn from about 1700, listed Grade I.

HAY-STL.name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha
HAY-STL.text: Your train passes near Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha, on the train's {side}. When it opened in 2003, Guinness World Records named it the largest Sikh temple outside India.

HAN-STL.name: Wharncliffe Viaduct
HAN-STL.text: Your train crosses the Wharncliffe Viaduct over the Brent valley, Isambard Kingdom Brunel's first major design for the railway, built in 1836 and 1837. Lord Wharncliffe's coat of arms is carved on its south side.

EAL-WEA.name: Pitzhanger Manor
EAL-WEA.text: Your train passes near Pitzhanger Manor, on the train's {side}, the country house that the architect Sir John Soane designed and built for himself between 1800 and 1804.

HAN-WEA.name: Kensington and Chelsea Cemetery, Hanwell
HAN-WEA.text: Your train passes near the Kensington and Chelsea cemetery in Hanwell, on the train's {side}, opened in 1855. One of its tombs, for the shell expert Edgar Smith, is decorated with a large conch shell.
